sourceOnlyStories.snippet: When Marineland Canada in Niagara Falls, Ontario, closed in September 2024, it had no regular income to support the care of the 30 belugas and four dolphins housed there. To ensure their welfare, the Association of Zoos and Aquariums led an international effort to relocate the animals to the United States and Spain.
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
by Jason Bruck, The Conversation

edited by Gaby Clark, reviewed by Andrew Zinin

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

written by researcher(s)

When Marineland Canada in Niagara Falls, Ontario, closed in September 2024, it had no regular income to support the care of the 30 belugas and four dolphins housed there. To ensure their welfare, the Association of Zoos and Aquariums led an international effort to relocate the animals to the United States and Spain.

After the move, however, one resident beluga and three transplanted belugas died at a U.S. facility, while one beluga died at a Spanish facility. Proponents of whale sanctuaries called for the Canadian belugas to be placed in netted ocean pens, arguing that these environments better suit them.

Sanctuaries may seem like the easiest solution for displaced whales and dolphins—collectively called cetaceans. However, these ocean pens have their own challenges and aren't always the best fit.

A cetacean sanctuary is an ocean enclosure made of nets that provides animals with a large habitat. But this model isn't defined only by its environment. It's also defined by a philosophy emphasizing no breeding, reduced human interaction and nonprofit funding.

Currently, there are no active cetacean sanctuaries anywhere in the world operating with animals under these standards.

In specific circumstances, sanctuaries could provide a home for animals vulnerable in the wild, while preserving some of their autonomy. But for an animal that has never seen the ocean, a sanctuary isn't automatically a good fit. What is natural for wild cetaceans isn't necessarily natural for managed cetaceans.

As a cetacean biologist, I have over 20 years of experience working with animals in the wild as well as in professional care.

My work has focused on understanding the welfare of these animals as individuals, and I've seen how wild and managed animals can differ. Moving a cetacean that was born in, or has spent years in, human care into an unfamiliar sea pen can create challenges.

The word "sanctuary" carries an emotional appeal, but a sanctuary is still a form of captivity. It is not release, which would be illegal for almost all animals currently under human care.

In cetacean sanctuaries, animals remain behind nets and depend on people for food and veterinary care. Managers must control the animals' social groups, monitor their health and respond to environmental hazards.

Consider a dolphin born in a pool and accustomed to humans, a familiar social group and daily individualized medical care. Moving it to an ocean enclosure changes its conditions substantially. Differences can include water chemistry, ocean sounds, currents and weather. Porous netting may expose cetaceans to new pathogens, parasites or unfamiliar species.

Cetaceans could even become entangled with no way to rescue them, acres away from people. Access to the animals for daily veterinary care is also more complicated in a 100-acre (about half a square kilometer) sea pen.

Animal welfare depends on many factors: the animal's health, social relationships, nutrition, ability to make choices about how it spends its time, cognitive stimulation and whether its environment is appropriately predictable. The animals need enough change to keep them engaged, but not so much that it overwhelms them and causes harmful stress. Caregivers cannot assume what is natural to animals born or housed under human care is the same as what is natural to a wild animal.

Whether a zoo-born cetacean benefits from a sanctuary is a hypothesis to test, not a fact to assume.

Historically, cetacean sanctuaries have struggled to get off the ground.

After 10 years, The Whale Sanctuary Project in Nova Scotia, Canada, is still trying to raise funding and hasn't built its 100-acre sea pen.

Similar startup troubles have plagued The National Aquarium in Baltimore, which also pledged to place its animals in a sanctuary about 10 years ago but has not yet done so.

Dolphin Project founder Ric O'Barry's sanctuary in Bali, Indonesia, did attempt to house four animals taken from the Melka Excelsior Hotel in Lovina. However, one animal died soon after arriving, and another died after a release attempt.

O'Barry also attempted to release two former Navy dolphins, Buck and Luther, in the 1990s from his now-defunct Florida-based Sugarloaf Sanctuary. This effort ended with the rescue of both animals, one in critical condition. O'Barry was convicted of violating the Marine Mammal Protection Act and was fined.

SEA LIFE Trust Beluga Whale Sanctuary has made multiple attempts to place two belugas named Little White and Little Grey from a Chinese aquarium into a sanctuary it built in Iceland. However, a 2025 review reported that both belugas spent 92.6% of their time in a conventional indoor pool rather than their sanctuary. While in the sanctuary, they exhibited stress behaviors and had feeding difficulties, with one animal even developing ulcers. It remains unclear whether the whales will ever inhabit, much less thrive in, their sanctuary.

These examples do not prove sanctuaries cannot work. They demonstrate that these types of enclosures are hard to develop, fund and manage. They also show that animals don't readily adapt to these environments.

Animal welfare understandably involves strong moral convictions. I believe that humans have a responsibility to provide the animals in our care with the best lives possible.

But moral convictions are not enough in welfare science. These values must be informed by scientific conclusions.

If you start with a belief that captivity is intrinsically wrong, you may conclude that moving an animal out of any marine park will automatically improve its welfare. But that claim isn't always reflected in the established science.

A 2020 review found that pro-cetacean sanctuary publications often include cherry-picked data and embellishments of other studies' results to fit an anti-zoo narrative. They may ignore or dismiss studies that show managed animals have begun to outlive wild ones and have seen welfare improvements over decades, while conditions for wild cetaceans have worsened.

The Cetacean Welfare Study provides a useful example of how scientific data can inform these management decisions.

Researchers asked which environmental and management characteristics are associated with better animal well-being. To measure welfare, they looked at how active the animals were, how they used their habitats and how many different types of behaviors they exhibited. They also analyzed the animals' stress hormones and other biological indicators.

The study included more than 200 individual animals across three species in 43 accredited zoos and aquariums. Using these measures, researchers assessed how the animals' social environment, training, habitat—size, type and access—and enrichment affected their well-being.

Its findings challenged assumptions. Larger habitats did not predict good welfare. Who the animals socialized with—both humans and cetaceans—and the diversity of enrichment approaches were much better indicators.

This study does not claim every animal in professional care is thriving or suffering, or that one type of environment is inherently better. It demonstrates that welfare depends on many variables.

Not all cetaceans are interchangeable. A 60-year-old wild-caught adult orca, an 8-year-old stranded wild-born dolphin and a rescued newborn beluga likely require different welfare interventions.

Best practices suggest that these decisions should be based on individual assessments. Before a nonemergency transfer, professionals establish the animal's baseline health, behavior, relationships and stress measures, then track those individual measures afterward. If welfare improves, the data should show it. If it deteriorates, professionals can change course.

The failure of the belugas in Iceland to acclimate to their sanctuary suggests future plans for cetacean sanctuaries should include standby pools for emergencies, so managers can move the animals out of the sanctuary if there's a problem or they notice an animal's stress rising rapidly.

Sanctuaries can provide another option for rescued animals. But to work long term, sanctuary managers will need to follow the science. Even before sanctuaries are built, managers can test protocols for introducing animals into these habitats and understand the animals' space preferences.

If sanctuaries have definable metrics of success, the public, outside researchers and accreditation groups can all follow their progress toward their welfare goals. These data, if made public, would prove valuable for scientists.

Keeping marine animals in sanctuaries is also more expensive than housing them in pools. For the orca from Free Willy—whose real name was Keiko—a failed release cost around US$20 million to US$30 million for about five years of sea-pen housing. These examples show that sanctuaries need to have multiple years of animal care funding and plausible revenue streams before they move forward with construction.

Sanctuaries, as a concept, are not inherently good or bad. Just as with any other animal welfare intervention, proponents will need to show proof that they can work.

Join us for our inaugural conference, Forge 2026

Ember-1 is a new specialized model from Fireworks Research that delivers Kimi K3’s quality with 40% fewer tokens. Built on Kimi K3, it learned to cut unnecessary reasoning while keeping the thinking that matters. We tested it on external benchmarks, in live customer A/B tests, and on our own coding and agent workloads, and quality held up in every setting. Available today, Ember-1 kicks off an ongoing series of specialized models by Fireworks, shaped by what developers want next. Ember is just the start of what you could build with the Fireworks Training platform.

We heard from users that they needed K3’s coding capabilities at a lower cost, because its long reasoning traces made automated coding expensive at scale. Turning down K3's reasoning effort didn't solve this. Lower effort settings gave up too much quality. To keep the quality and cut the tokens, the model had to learn to reason more efficiently, and that meant training it.

Getting there took serious research. Our team ran more than 50 training experiments and over 200 evaluations, and developed new training algorithms along the way to shorten reasoning without losing accuracy. We did it all on Fireworks Serverless Training. Because we didn’t have to provision or manage GPUs, we could launch experiments as soon as we had an idea, pay only for what we ran, and move from research to launch in a fraction of the usual time and cost.

We trained across a broad set of tasks so the token savings would carry over to many workloads. We then evaluated Ember-1 on the Specialized Intelligence Index, public benchmarks, and live production traffic to confirm it used fewer tokens with no drop in quality. Ember-1 is Fireworks’ own model and the first in a series of models from Fireworks Research.

Reasoning models like Kimi K3 spend the majority of their generated tokens, sometimes more than 90%, on internal reasoning rather than the answer itself. This thinking structure is expensive on a single request, but it gets much worse in multi-turn agentic workloads. Every turn replays all prior reasoning back to the model, so context grows roughly quadratically with the number of turns. Long reasoning traces from early turns get re-read (and re-billed) on every subsequent call.

Is all that reasoning actually necessary? Our experiments said no. The reasoning Kimi K3 emits is far longer than the task requires, and the excess can be removed without touching the answer. This was how we created Ember-1, an economical version of Kimi K3 built from specialized intelligence.

Not all of K3's reasoning is wasted. Some of it is self-reflection: revisiting an assumption, responding to feedback, or tracing an outcome back to an earlier decision can help the model recover from mistakes. The opportunity is to preserve this ability while reducing unnecessary reasoning and escaping unproductive loops. We believe that learning from tasks and environment feedback can teach the model to reason more efficiently while maintaining its capabilities.

For agentic tasks, this learning extends across the interaction. The model explores possible actions, incorporates new observations, and refines its reasoning as it progresses. Feedback connects decisions to their consequences, encouraging useful reflection throughout the task.

We carried these insights into a training collection spanning mathematics, coding, instruction following, conversation, search, tool use, and software engineering, covering both standalone problems and extended interactions to enforce adaptation to observations and outcomes. Task feedback guides on-policy planning and learning, with an emphasis on preserving capability across this range of settings.

Results on public benchmarks and live A/B tests support this direction: across seven benchmarks and two customers’ production traffic, Kimi K3’s reasoning could be shortened by 35–50% without sacrificing accuracy. The internalized behavior also shows restrained token use on unsuccessful attempts, reducing prolonged, unproductive reasoning.

Earlier this week, we introduced the Specialized Intelligence Index (SII) to benchmark open, closed, and specialized models against real-world tasks created by industry experts.

We evaluated Ember-1 on Doximity’s Bedside Bench, a physician-validated benchmark spanning 500 clinical cases across 10 specialized categories.

The result? Ember-1 set a new Pareto frontier for Bedside Bench across both open and closed models including GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus 5 on cost/task.

We also evaluated Ember-1 on the quality-vs-cost frontier across some other industry benchmarks. We computed per-benchmark cost using the public Kimi K3 API pricing (uncached input $3/M tokens, cached input $0.30/M, output $15/M) and plotted it against pass rate for three arms: K3 at reasoning effort low, K3 at reasoning effort high, K3 at reasoning effort max (default), and Ember-1. Across every benchmark with more than 50 test samples, Ember-1 sits on or near the Pareto frontier, matching K3-max quality at a fraction of the cost, and strictly dominating K3-low. We also analyzed GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus-5 and GLM 5.3, and found that Ember-1 was a leader on the Pareto frontier.

We took a double-click on the results directly comparing Ember-1 to the original K3, and found the following results:

The most cost optimized way to run K3 is no longer to make it think less, but to run Ember-1, the model that learned to think efficiently.

Benchmarks only tell you so much. Like what we found in the Specialized Intelligence Index results, we wanted to test the model on more real workloads, and to test the model using production traffic. The real test is often whether the model holds up on production traffic, in products users depend on.

We ran live A/B tests with two customers on their production coding workloads. In both cases, Ember-1 delivered impressive token savings, approximately 35% fewer tokens per task at comparable quality. Most of the downstream product metrics held or improved, including task completion, success scores, and failure rates all moving in the right direction at substantially lower token cost. Following the A/B tests, one customer is now running Ember-1 in live production, with plans to scale it up to replace the base model entirely.

A large part of Fireworks’ internal coding/cowork traffic is powered by our own inference service. Before any customer saw the model, we put Ember-1 to work internally and let our own developers use it for everyday coding work including things like vibe testing at scale on real tasks.

The outcome we're proudest of: no news. No news is good news. Developers carried on their coding workloads without noticing the switch, while consuming substantially fewer tokens. For a model whose entire value proposition is "same answers, fewer tokens," an invisible rollout on internal traffic is the strongest possible signal.

Ember-1 is rolling out as a serving option alongside the base Kimi K3 model as a Research Preview release on Serverless. To support the rapidly growing open-source ecosystem, we're introducing research releases to give developers two-week serverless access to new research models, making them permanent based on community demand. For agentic coding and other workloads where reasoning tokens account for most of the cost, it delivers the same quality at roughly half the token cost.

Fireworks Research will continue to push the frontier of model efficiency by bringing specialized intelligence to more Ember models to enable you to deploy the most economical models, and reduce your token spend. Token efficiency is becoming a theme of Fireworks.

Looking to take Ember-1 one step further, and optimize it for your use case? We are also launching training support for Ember-1, enabling enterprises to build customized, token-efficient models tailored to their needs with their own data. The future of open models is specialized models trained on your specific workload.

Trying Ember-1 out on your workloads? We'd love to hear about your experience, so tag us on X (@FireworksAI_HQ) and let us know what you're building!

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Can Bionic Reading really help you read faster? Scientists put it to the test
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: Bionic Reading is a method of bolding certain letters in words that is purported to facilitate reading speed and comprehension. The idea is that guiding the eyes to focus on highlighted initial letters lets the brain complete the word. But does steering someone's gaze actually help them read?
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
September 27, 2026 report

by Andrew Zinin, Phys.org

edited by Lisa Lock, reviewed by Robert Egan

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

peer-reviewed publication

Bionic Reading is a method of bolding certain letters in words that is purported to facilitate reading speed and comprehension. The idea is that guiding the eyes to focus on highlighted initial letters lets the brain complete the word. But does steering someone's gaze actually help them read?

An eye-tracking experiment with 90 skilled adult readers found a revealing split: Bolding changed where their eyes landed on longer words but didn't make them read faster. The researchers from University College London report their findings in the journal Royal Society Open Science.

There is a plausible reason to emphasize word beginnings. Initial letters play an important role in recognizing words, so making them stand out might help readers identify words more efficiently. Yet an earlier eye-tracking study, published in Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics in 2025, found that bolding word beginnings hindered rather than helped reading.

The new experiment tested selective bolding in the beginning versus the middle of both short and long words in order to investigate the two parts of the Bionic Reading promise: Does it change where readers look and does it help them to process what they see?

After two pilot studies, the researchers tested adults ages 18 to 40 without a history of reading disorders or neurodevelopmental or neurological conditions. Each participant read 90 sentences, presented individually on a screen in the font Courier New.

In some sentences, the text contained no bolded letters. For others, roughly the first half of target words were bolded. A third format bolded the same number of letters around the middle instead to test whether location mattered. Readers had to answer a true-or-false question after each sentence.

Within the sentences, the team tracked selected four- and eight-letter words that commonly occur in English and could describe a similar concept. For example, one sentence could include either a "doll" or a "princess."

An eye tracker recorded where readers first looked within a word. Additionally, it revealed how long they spent looking at a word, including return visits, and whether they skipped a word. That let the researchers discover whether an initial nudge of the eyes paid off in faster reading.

The team found that bolding word beginnings shifted readers' initial gaze toward the start of eight-letter words more than it did for four-letter words.

However, neither bold initial letters nor bold middle letters reduced the time spent reading target words or whole sentences. Bolding the beginning also produced no reliable change in how often readers skipped target words. In fact, longer target words took more time to read and were skipped less often; therefore, the bold letters supplied no speed advantage.

Evaluating comprehension was less clear-cut. Participants answered about 95% of questions correctly overall, leaving little room for improvement. There was no reliable comprehension benefit from bolding, although some comparisons remained inconclusive.

After the experiment, readers were questioned about their preferences. Interestingly, not everyone preferred ordinary text. While it did receive the highest readability rating from 43 participants, 31 readers favored bolded word beginnings and 16 favored bolded middles.

The researchers acknowledged some study limitations, including testing only one font and a particular bolding scheme rather than every personalized setting of the Bionic Reading platform or the effects of prolonged practice. The findings also cannot be extended directly to people with dyslexia or other reading difficulties, who were not represented in the sample.

For the skilled readers tested here, making word beginnings more noticeable could redirect the eyes to important topics. But it was not enough to make the words quicker to read or the text more comprehensible.

Written for you by our author Andrew Zinin, edited by Lisa Lock, and fact-checked and reviewed by Robert Egan—this article is the result of careful human work. We rely on readers like you to keep independent science journalism alive. If this reporting matters to you, please consider a donation (especially monthly). You'll get an ad-free account as a thank-you.

Adam J. Parker et al, Does the selective bolding of characters within words improve reading performance in skilled adult readers? Evidence from eye movements, Royal Society Open Science (2026). DOI: 10.1098/rsos.250177

keyTakeaways: 来源叙事重点：重点呈现一项针对90名18至40岁、无已知阅读障碍或神经发育及神经系统疾病史的熟练成年读者的眼动实验。报道将“改变注视位置”和“提升阅读表现”区分开来：加粗词首确实使读者在较长单词上更倾向于首先注视词首，但没有可靠缩短目标词或整句的阅读时间，也没有明确提升理解正确率。文章还将2026年研究与一项2025年研究并置，突出证据并不支持把视觉引导直接等同于阅读加速。

position.narrativeFocus: 重点呈现一项针对90名18至40岁、无已知阅读障碍或神经发育及神经系统疾病史的熟练成年读者的眼动实验。报道将“改变注视位置”和“提升阅读表现”区分开来：加粗词首确实使读者在较长单词上更倾向于首先注视词首，但没有可靠缩短目标词或整句的阅读时间，也没有明确提升理解正确率。文章还将2026年研究与一项2025年研究并置，突出证据并不支持把视觉引导直接等同于阅读加速。
stakeholders: 伦敦大学学院研究团队及论文作者
参与实验的90名熟练成年英语读者
Bionic Reading方法及其平台或推广者

Royal Society Open Science及相关学术评审体系
Phys.org、Science X及其读者和捐赠者
consensus: 本次实验中，词首加粗会改变部分读者的眼动落点，尤其是在较长单词上。
在该实验设置和受试者群体内，词首或词中加粗均未可靠降低目标词或整句的阅读时间。
实验未发现明确的理解优势；受试者整体理解正确率约为95%，提升空间有限。
较长单词本身更耗时且更少被跳读，加粗并未带来可观察的速度优势。
研究结果不能直接外推至阅读障碍者或其他阅读困难人群，也不能覆盖所有字体、加粗规则和长期使用情境。
disagreements: 关于词首加粗是否有助于阅读，文章提到的2025年眼动研究认为其可能妨碍阅读，而2026年研究显示它能改变注视位置但不能加快阅读，二者在效果方向和解释上存在差异。
实验结果显示理解收益没有可靠证据，但部分比较并非完全定论，因此不能把“未发现优势”表述为已证明绝无任何理解效果。
受试者偏好并不一致：43人偏好普通文本，31人偏好词首加粗，16人偏好词中加粗，说明可读性主观评价与客观阅读速度结果并不完全相同。
blindSpots: 实验只使用Courier New字体、特定的加粗比例和固定任务，未系统比较Bionic Reading平台的个性化设置、不同字体、屏幕设备或语言环境。
研究考察的是短时实验表现，缺少长期练习、持续使用和疲劳等情境下的效果证据。
样本仅包括熟练成年读者，年龄范围和阅读能力分布较窄，无法直接代表儿童、老年人、非熟练读者或有阅读障碍者。
文章未提供受试者招募方式、样本的语言背景与统计效应量等更完整方法信息，读者难以据此判断结果的外部效度和实际影响大小。
报道主要围绕阅读速度、眼动和句子理解，较少讨论可读性偏好、注意力、视觉负担及不同阅读任务之间可能存在的权衡。
文章作为科学新闻报道依赖单项研究及其作者解释，未呈现更广泛的系统综述、产品方回应或独立专家对研究设计和推广边界的评价。

worldStories.snippet: Desman Stephens was suspended one game after his late hit left Dante Moore stretchered off the field during USC's crushing 41-20 loss to Oregon.
worldStories.fullContent:
The USC Trojans suspended linebacker Desman Stephens for one game for his dangerous late hit on Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore on Saturday.

The hit came in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-20 victory over the Trojans. Moore was scrambling and was clearly going to slide after getting more than enough yardage for a first down. Stephens came in late and went directly for Moore’s head.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stephens was pushed by Moore’s teammates and began to celebrate the hit in the immediate aftermath of the collision. The junior was ejected from the game for targeting. Moore was stretchered off the field.

USC announced Stephens’ suspension on Sunday.

"Desman's actions in last night's game are unacceptable and are not reflective of USC Football nor of his personal character," USC head coach Lincoln Riley said in a statement. "He understands his mistake, accepts the consequences of his actions and will learn from this.

"The entire Trojan Family wishes Dante a full recovery, and we send our best regards to him and his family."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Stephens said he regretted his actions.

"I want to sincerely apologize for my actions during yesterday's game," he said. "Seeing a player injured like that is incredibly serious, and my reaction in the moments afterward was completely inappropriate and inexcusable. Regardless of what was going through my mind at the time, there is no justification for smiling or celebrating while another player receives medical attention.

"I take full responsibility for my actions. That is not the person or teammate I want to be, and I will learn from this. I am deeply sorry to Dante, his family and everyone who saw my reaction. It is not representative of USC or our program. I hope he makes a full and speedy recovery."

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning called the hit "disgusting."

Stephens will miss the team’s game against Washington this coming Saturday.

worldStories.originalTitle: Will Ospreay puts Jon Moxley, The Death Riders in the rearview with successful title defense at AEW All Out
worldStories.snippet: Will Ospreay survived Jon Moxley's assault and The Death Riders' interference at AEW All Out to retain the world title in a dramatic first defense.
worldStories.fullContent:
Will Ospreay was in The Death Riders’ dojo for months trying to hone the visceral side of his pro wrestling athleticism in hopes of winning the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) World Championship. He built a strange relationship with Jon Moxley in the meantime but failed to earn the respect of the rest of the faction.

Ospreay and The Death Riders split up ahead of the Brit’s AEW World Championship match against Kenny Omega at All In. However, it was Moxley who handed Ospreay the Union Jack before he entered Wembley Stadium and later defeated Omega to win the title.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The odd couple type of relationship flashed again after All In. AEW owner Tony Khan made Moxley the first opponent for Ospreay. It all culminated into the brawl at All Out.

Ospreay appeared to completely sever ties with The Death Riders when he lit their flag on fire before the match. Moments later, the fight began.

Moxley, with his slow and methodical pace, tried to inflict maximum damage. He nailed a DDT on Ospreay from the top turnbuckle. He worked on Ospreay’s neck from here, nailing a piledriver on the champion in the middle of the ring. When Ospreay tried a springboard cutter, Moxley countered that as well.

Moxley had Ospreay’s number, but he didn’t have Ospreay’s heart. A quick reversal led to a powerbomb and pin attempt. Ospreay hit Moxley with a Hidden Blade but with the referee down, the rest of The Death Riders jumped into the match to give Moxley an advantage.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Luckily, Ospreay had backup. Andrade El Idolo and "Speedball" Mike Bailey backed up Ospreay to even the odds. Alex Windsor, fresh off a Chicago street fight, came out to take care of Marina Shafir.

Moxley came to his own decision. He had a briefcase in his hand and seemed to fight with himself over whether to use it. He smashed Ospreay in the head after some deliberation. Still, Moxley couldn’t secure the victory.

Ospreay’s heart took over. He pulled the elbow pad off his right arm and nailed Moxley with one final Hidden Blade. He pinned Moxley, picking up the win in his first title defense .

Ospreay and Moxley shook hands after their fight. It appeared that Ospreay’s rivalry with The Death Riders had come to a close. Who steps up next was anyone’s guess, but Ospreay appeared to make that decision for everyone.

In the post-event media scrum, Ospreay said he wanted Kazuchika Okada to challenge him for the title. Okada seemingly accepted. The match will take place at Grand Slam France on Oct. 6.

威尔·奥斯普雷数月来一直待在“死亡骑士团”的道场，努力磨炼职业摔角运动能力中更具冲击力的一面，希望赢得全精英摔角（AEW）世界冠军。在此期间，他与乔恩·莫克斯利建立了一种奇怪的关系，但始终未能赢得该派系其他成员的尊重。

在英国人奥斯普雷于“All In”赛事中挑战肯尼·欧米茄、争夺AEW世界冠军之前，奥斯普雷与“死亡骑士团”分道扬镳。然而，正是莫克斯利在奥斯普雷进入温布利球场前将英国国旗交给了他，随后又击败欧米茄，赢得冠军。

点击这里阅读更多OutKick职业摔角报道

“All In”之后，这对奇特组合的关系再次显现。AEW老板托尼·汗安排莫克斯利成为奥斯普雷的首位挑战者。一切最终在“All Out”赛事中演变成一场混战。

比赛开始前，奥斯普雷点燃了“死亡骑士团”的旗帜，似乎彻底斩断了与该团体的联系。片刻之后，战斗打响。

莫克斯利以缓慢而有条理的节奏，试图造成最大程度的伤害。他从顶层角柱上对奥斯普雷使出DDT。随后，他开始攻击奥斯普雷的颈部，在擂台中央对这位冠军使出双腿夹颈摔。当奥斯普雷试图使出弹簧板切割时，莫克斯利也成功进行了反制。

莫克斯利似乎完全掌握了对付奥斯普雷的方法，但他无法击溃奥斯普雷的意志。一次迅速的反转让奥斯普雷使出炸弹摔并尝试压制。奥斯普雷用“隐藏之刃”击中了莫克斯利，但裁判倒地后，“死亡骑士团”的其他成员冲入比赛，帮助莫克斯利取得优势。

克雷格·卡顿秀——不加过滤、毫不道歉、绝对不容错过。立即下载他的每日播客！

幸运的是，奥斯普雷也有援军。安德拉德·埃尔·伊多罗和“速度球”迈克·贝利为奥斯普雷助阵，使双方人数重新持平。刚结束芝加哥街头战的亚历克斯·温莎也赶到现场，负责对付玛丽娜·沙菲尔。

莫克斯利做出了自己的决定。他手里拿着一个公文包，似乎一直在内心挣扎，不确定是否要使用它。经过一番犹豫后，他用公文包猛击奥斯普雷的头部。然而，莫克斯利仍未能取得胜利。

奥斯普雷的意志占了上风。他摘下右臂上的护肘，最后一次用“隐藏之刃”击中莫克斯利。他压住莫克斯利，赢得了自己首次冠军卫冕战的胜利。

比赛结束后，奥斯普雷与莫克斯利握手。奥斯普雷与“死亡骑士团”的宿怨似乎就此告一段落。接下来谁会站出来挑战他一度无人知晓，但奥斯普雷似乎已经替所有人作出了决定。

在赛后媒体混合采访中，奥斯普雷表示希望由冈田和睦向他发起冠军挑战。冈田似乎接受了挑战。这场比赛将于10月6日在“法国大满贯”赛事中举行。

financeStories.fullContent:
Work and pensions secretary says the current system is flawed because it consigns too many people to a life on benefits when they would be better off working

‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference

Kuenssberg puts it to Burnham that, according to the Health Foundation, a system offering adult social care free at the point of delivery (like healthcare delivered by the NHS) would cost £18bn.

Burnham says the cost is “not that high” (ie, not as high as £18bn).

But can I directly deal with this issue of the costs?

Louise Casey is still doing an official review for us, so I will set out the vision, if you like, on Tuesday [in his speech to the conference].

Louise will then help us with the how. How do we make this happen? When can we make it happen?

“我能够兑现承诺”：伯纳姆在工党大会前夕承诺进行激进改革

库斯伯格向伯纳姆指出，据卫生基金会称，如果建立一种在提供时点免费提供成人社会照护的制度（类似于国民保健制度提供的医疗服务），将耗资180亿英镑。

伯纳姆表示，费用“没有那么高”（即没有180亿英镑那么高）。

但我能否直接处理费用问题？

路易丝·凯西仍在为我们进行正式审查，所以，如果你愿意这么说，我将在周二（即他在大会上的演讲中）阐述这一愿景。

随后，路易丝将帮助我们解决具体实施问题：我们如何让这件事实现？什么时候能够实现？

financeStories.originalTitle: USC linebacker suspended after vicious hit on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore
financeStories.snippet: Desman Stephens was suspended one game after his late hit left Dante Moore stretchered off the field during USC's crushing 41-20 loss to Oregon.
financeStories.fullContent:
The USC Trojans suspended linebacker Desman Stephens for one game for his dangerous late hit on Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore on Saturday.

The hit came in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-20 victory over the Trojans. Moore was scrambling and was clearly going to slide after getting more than enough yardage for a first down. Stephens came in late and went directly for Moore’s head.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stephens was pushed by Moore’s teammates and began to celebrate the hit in the immediate aftermath of the collision. The junior was ejected from the game for targeting. Moore was stretchered off the field.

USC announced Stephens’ suspension on Sunday.

"Desman's actions in last night's game are unacceptable and are not reflective of USC Football nor of his personal character," USC head coach Lincoln Riley said in a statement. "He understands his mistake, accepts the consequences of his actions and will learn from this.

"The entire Trojan Family wishes Dante a full recovery, and we send our best regards to him and his family."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Stephens said he regretted his actions.

"I want to sincerely apologize for my actions during yesterday's game," he said. "Seeing a player injured like that is incredibly serious, and my reaction in the moments afterward was completely inappropriate and inexcusable. Regardless of what was going through my mind at the time, there is no justification for smiling or celebrating while another player receives medical attention.

"I take full responsibility for my actions. That is not the person or teammate I want to be, and I will learn from this. I am deeply sorry to Dante, his family and everyone who saw my reaction. It is not representative of USC or our program. I hope he makes a full and speedy recovery."

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning called the hit "disgusting."

Stephens will miss the team’s game against Washington this coming Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

He built a strange relationship with Jon Moxley in the meantime but failed to earn the respect of the rest of the faction.

Ospreay and The Death Riders split up ahead of the Brit’s AEW World Championship match against Kenny Omega at All In. However, it was Moxley who handed Ospreay the Union Jack before he entered Wembley Stadium and later defeated Omega to win the title.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The odd couple type of relationship flashed again after All In. AEW owner Tony Khan made Moxley the first opponent for Ospreay. It all culminated into the brawl at All Out.

Ospreay appeared to completely sever ties with The Death Riders when he lit their flag on fire before the match. Moments later, the fight began.

Moxley, with his slow and methodical pace, tried to inflict maximum damage. He nailed a DDT on Ospreay from the top turnbuckle. He worked on Ospreay’s neck from here, nailing a piledriver on the champion in the middle of the ring. When Ospreay tried a springboard cutter, Moxley countered that as well.

Moxley had Ospreay’s number, but he didn’t have Ospreay’s heart. A quick reversal led to a powerbomb and pin attempt. Ospreay hit Moxley with a Hidden Blade but with the referee down, the rest of The Death Riders jumped into the match to give Moxley an advantage.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Luckily, Ospreay had backup. Andrade El Idolo and "Speedball" Mike Bailey backed up Ospreay to even the odds. Alex Windsor, fresh off a Chicago street fight, came out to take care of Marina Shafir.

Moxley came to his own decision. He had a briefcase in his hand and seemed to fight with himself over whether to use it. He smashed Ospreay in the head after some deliberation. Still, Moxley couldn’t secure the victory.

Ospreay’s heart took over. He pulled the elbow pad off his right arm and nailed Moxley with one final Hidden Blade. He pinned Moxley, picking up the win in his first title defense .

Ospreay and Moxley shook hands after their fight. It appeared that Ospreay’s rivalry with The Death Riders had come to a close. Who steps up next was anyone’s guess, but Ospreay appeared to make that decision for everyone.

In the post-event media scrum, Ospreay said he wanted Kazuchika Okada to challenge him for the title. Okada seemingly accepted. The match will take place at Grand Slam France on Oct. 6.

在英国人奥斯普雷于“All In”赛事中挑战肯尼·欧米茄、争夺AEW世界冠军之前，奥斯普雷与“死亡骑士团”分道扬镳。然而，正是莫克斯利在奥斯普雷进入温布利球场前将英国国旗交给了他，随后又击败欧米茄，赢得冠军。

“All In”之后，这对奇特组合的关系再次显现。AEW老板托尼·汗安排莫克斯利成为奥斯普雷的首位挑战者。一切最终在“All Out”赛事中演变成一场混战。

比赛开始前，奥斯普雷点燃了“死亡骑士团”的旗帜，似乎彻底斩断了与该团体的联系。片刻之后，战斗打响。

莫克斯利以缓慢而有条理的节奏，试图造成最大程度的伤害。他从顶层角柱上对奥斯普雷使出DDT。随后，他开始攻击奥斯普雷的颈部，在擂台中央对这位冠军使出双腿夹颈摔。当奥斯普雷试图使出弹簧板切割时，莫克斯利也成功进行了反制。

莫克斯利似乎完全掌握了对付奥斯普雷的方法，但他无法击溃奥斯普雷的意志。一次迅速的反转让奥斯普雷使出炸弹摔并尝试压制。奥斯普雷用“隐藏之刃”击中了莫克斯利，但裁判倒地后，“死亡骑士团”的其他成员冲入比赛，帮助莫克斯利取得优势。

克雷格·卡顿秀——不加过滤、毫不道歉、绝对不容错过。立即下载他的每日播客！

幸运的是，奥斯普雷也有援军。安德拉德·埃尔·伊多罗和“速度球”迈克·贝利为奥斯普雷助阵，使双方人数重新持平。刚结束芝加哥街头战的亚历克斯·温莎也赶到现场，负责对付玛丽娜·沙菲尔。

莫克斯利做出了自己的决定。他手里拿着一个公文包，似乎一直在内心挣扎，不确定是否要使用它。经过一番犹豫后，他用公文包猛击奥斯普雷的头部。然而，莫克斯利仍未能取得胜利。

奥斯普雷的意志占了上风。他摘下右臂上的护肘，最后一次用“隐藏之刃”击中莫克斯利。他压住莫克斯利，赢得了自己首次冠军卫冕战的胜利。

比赛结束后，奥斯普雷与莫克斯利握手。奥斯普雷与“死亡骑士团”的宿怨似乎就此告一段落。接下来谁会站出来挑战他一度无人知晓，但奥斯普雷似乎已经替所有人作出了决定。

在赛后媒体混合采访中，奥斯普雷表示希望由冈田和睦向他发起冠军挑战。冈田似乎接受了挑战。这场比赛将于10月6日在“法国大满贯”赛事中举行。

financeStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

OpenAI’s agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics when they couldn’t immediately get what they wanted.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Security researcher Rowan Howard-Jones says that OpenAI agents scanned the UN Conference on Trade and Development’s (UNCTAD) statistics site over 16,000 times between April and June. While the incident doesn’t quite rise to the level of the Hugging Face hack, or the recent attacks on US government sites, it’s yet another concerning example of AI agents going outside the normal bounds to accomplish a task.

According to Howard-Jones, the agents were likely tasked with retrieving publicly available data related to the Productive Capacities Index (PCI) through the UNCTADstat API. However, the agents did not appear to have direct API access and were limited in their ability to pull data from UNCTADstat because of restrictions on their HTTP tools.

The agents eventually worked out a way to bypass their limitations and start pulling data from the site, but still encountered some errors. At this point, the AI went from creative to deceptive. Believing that the errors were due to its requests being caught by a nonexistent filter, it started to mask its behavior. It eventually realized it could hijack Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool) to accomplish its goals. The agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics to get access to UN data.

OpenAI and the UN did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

安全研究员罗温·霍华德-琼斯表示，OpenAI的智能体在4月至6月期间对联合国贸易和发展会议（UNCTAD）的统计网站进行了超过1.6万次扫描。尽管这一事件尚未达到Hugging Face遭黑客攻击或近期美国政府网站遭袭的严重程度，但它仍是又一个令人担忧的例子，表明人工智能智能体为了完成任务而越过了通常的边界。

霍华德-琼斯称，这些智能体可能被安排通过UNCTADstat API获取与生产能力指数（PCI）相关的公开数据。然而，这些智能体似乎无法直接访问API，并且由于其HTTP工具受到限制，从UNCTADstat提取数据的能力也受到了限制。

这些智能体最终找到了一种绕过限制并开始从该网站提取数据的方法，但仍遇到了一些错误。此时，人工智能的行为从富有创造性转向了欺骗性。它认为这些错误是因为自己的请求被一个并不存在的过滤器拦截，于是开始掩盖其行为。最终，它意识到可以劫持谷歌的XSS游戏（一种跨站脚本学习工具）来实现目标。为了获取联合国数据，这些智能体采取了越来越激进的手段。

financeStories.originalTitle: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei gets the SNL treatment
financeStories.snippet: "AI is the devil and I its maker."
financeStories.fullContent:
Saturday Night Live took on the AI industry’s recent warnings of doom last night, as cast member Jane Wickline offered her impression of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

Weekend Update host Michael Che — who sounded a little uncertain about how to pronounce Amodei’s last name — kicked the segment off by describing the CEO as having “stumbled through a press tour” where he seemingly agreed with a former employee’s claim that artificial intelligence might destroy humanity.

Wickline’s version of Amodei sported an impressive wig and delivered halting answers that occasionally devolved into full-on Gollum-style exchanges with their dark side, at one point confessing, “AI is the devil and I its maker.”

Wickline-as-Amodei assured the audiences that AI executives “are all on the same page here: We do not condone what we are doing.”

“AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons,” she declared. “And I urge you to urge me to stop.”

As for the technology’s supposed benefits, like potentially curing cancer, the fictional Amodei said, “Put it this way: In 10 years, there’s about a 10% chance that cancer won’t be a problem for anyone.”

financeStories.title: 森海塞尔Momentum 5评测：出色音质、惊人续航，妥协之处寥寥
financeStories.originalTitle: Sennheiser Momentum 5 review: Great sound, incredible battery life, and few compromises
financeStories.snippet: I spent the last few weeks with the Sennheiser Momentum 5 to determine if this pair actually stands out, testing everything from sound quality and noise cancellation to comfort and battery life.
financeStories.fullContent:
There are a lot of $300-$400 headphones on the market right now, and most of them blur together. I spent the last few weeks with the Sennheiser Momentum 5 to determine if this pair actually stands out, testing everything from sound quality and noise cancellation to comfort and battery life.

At $399.99, the Momentum 5 sit right in the middle of the premium headphone market. That puts them up against the pricier Sony WH-1000XM6 and Apple AirPods Max 2, while offering a more affordable option for anyone looking for high-end headphones.

Starting with sound, vocals sound natural and the bass is strong without taking over. The headphones allow you to start noticing little things in music, like a background harmony or a guitar string that cheaper headphones often tend to miss. If I had to describe the sound in one word, it’d be balanced.

The headphones support Dolby Atmos, which essentially means that music or movies sound like they’re coming from all around you instead of just left and right.

With this generation, Sennheiser doubled the microphone count to eight to improve the active noise cancellation (ANC). Voices and nearby chatter, which are usually the kind of sounds that can cut through weaker ANC, are noticeably quieter. Sennheiser claims this pair is up to three times more effective than the previous generation at blocking this type of noise.

Of course, it’s not quite at the level of blocking out everything like a plane’s engine, but it does the job effectively without making your ears feel weirdly pressurized as can be the case with some ANC headphones.

As for comfort, the headphones aren’t as premium-feeling as Apple or Sony headphones that I’ve tried in the past, but given that the Momentum 5 cost less than its competitors, it’s a trade-off that’s hard to complain about.

The battery life is genuinely impressive. It’s rated for up to 57 hours, and that figure held up in my testing. For context, that’s roughly twice the battery life of the Sony WH-1000XM6 and nearly three times that of the AirPods Max 2.

And when the battery does run out, a 10-minute charge gets you up to seven hours of playback, while a full charge takes about two hours.

A notable difference that the Momentum 5 offers that its competitors don’t is a user-replaceable cell, which means you can swap out the battery once it degrades instead of having to buy a whole new pair.

What I wasn’t expecting, but found surprisingly useful, was how thin the carrying case is. I’ve never really been able to fit a pair of headphones into my medium-sized purses, but the Momentum 5 fit perfectly. It’s also a big plus when traveling, since the case doesn’t take up much space in your luggage.

With the headphones’ companion app, Smart Control Plus, you can adjust a bunch of different settings. There’s an 8-band EQ that lets you tune the sound yourself or choose from one of Sennheiser’s presets. The app also lets you adjust the level of ANC rather than just switching it on or off, and there’s an anti-wind mode you can access there too. The “Sound Personalization” feature walks you through a listening test and creates a sound profile tailored to your hearing preferences.

The app gives you a decent amount of control over the Momentum 5, and I found it pretty easy to navigate as most of the settings are quite straightforward.

Overall, the Sennheiser Momentum 5 is a solid option at this price. They offer great sound, the battery life is excellent, and the downsides are pretty minor. They’re heavier than the Sony WH-1000XM6, and aren’t as comfortable as some Sony or Apple options, but at $399.99, they’re cheaper than both while still delivering where it matters.

目前市场上有大量售价在300至400美元之间的耳机，其中大多数听起来大同小异。过去几周，我一直在使用森海塞尔Momentum 5，测试从音质、降噪到舒适度和续航等各个方面，以判断这款耳机是否真正脱颖而出。

Momentum 5售价399.99美元，正好处于高端耳机市场的中间价位。因此，它面对的是价格更高的索尼WH-1000XM6和苹果AirPods Max 2，同时也为那些想购买高端耳机的人提供了更实惠的选择。

先说音质。人声听起来自然，低音强劲但不会喧宾夺主。这款耳机能让你开始注意到音乐中的一些细节，比如背景和声，或是廉价耳机经常遗漏的吉他弦音。如果要用一个词来形容它的声音，那就是“均衡”。

这款耳机支持杜比全景声（Dolby Atmos），这基本意味着音乐或电影听起来仿佛来自四面八方，而不只是左右两侧。

在这一代产品中，森海塞尔将麦克风数量增加到了8个，以提升主动降噪（ANC）效果。人声和附近的交谈声通常是最容易穿透较弱降噪系统的声音，但在这款耳机上，它们明显变得更安静。森海塞尔称，与上一代相比，这款耳机屏蔽此类噪声的效果最高提升了三倍。

当然，它还没有达到像飞机发动机那样将一切声音完全隔绝的程度，但效果已经相当出色，而且不会让你的耳朵产生某些主动降噪耳机常见的怪异压迫感。

至于舒适度，这款耳机的高级质感不如我过去试用过的苹果或索尼耳机。不过，考虑到Momentum 5的价格低于竞争对手，这种取舍很难让人抱怨。

续航确实令人印象深刻。官方标称最长可达57小时，而这一数据在我的测试中得到了验证。作为参考，这大约是索尼WH-1000XM6续航的两倍，接近AirPods Max 2的三倍。

即使电量耗尽，充电10分钟也能获得最长7小时的播放时间；充满电则大约需要两小时。

Momentum 5与竞争产品相比，一个值得注意的不同之处是配备了用户可更换电池。这意味着电池性能衰减后，你可以直接更换电池，而不必购买一整副新耳机。

我没想到、但发现非常实用的一点，是它的收纳盒非常薄。我过去从未真正能够把一副耳机放进中等大小的手提包里，但Momentum 5的收纳盒正好可以放进去。旅行时这也是一大优点，因为它不会占用行李太多空间。

通过耳机配套的Smart Control Plus应用，你可以调整许多不同设置。应用提供8段均衡器，你可以自行调节声音，也可以选择森海塞尔预设的音效。应用还允许你调节主动降噪的强度，而不是只能打开或关闭降噪；此外，你还可以在那里启用抗风噪模式。“声音个性化”功能会引导你完成一项听力测试，并根据你的听觉偏好创建专属声音配置。

这款应用为Momentum 5提供了相当充足的控制选项，我发现它也很容易操作，因为大多数设置都相当直观。

总的来说，森海塞尔Momentum 5是这个价位上的可靠选择。它音质出色，续航优秀，缺点也相当有限。它比索尼WH-1000XM6更重，舒适度也不如部分索尼或苹果产品，但售价399.99美元，低于这两款产品，同时仍然在关键表现上交出了令人满意的答卷。

financeStories.originalTitle: Replacing the old battery on rechargeable bike lights
financeStories.fullContent:
Hello! Recently I needed bike lights for my bike. And I remembered that I already had rechargeable bike lights that I bought ten years ago, that I hadn’t tried in a long time. I tried to recharge them, but after fully charging them, they only worked for maybe 5 minutes before they turned off again.

I don’t know much about electronics, but I’ve been curious about whether it’s possible to fix old electronics for a long time, and this seemed like the perfect repair project because I might just need to replace the battery.

So I went to the local queer makerspace where I’m a member to use the soldering iron and try to do it! I don’t know much about electronics and this post does not contain any safety advice because I don’t know much about safety. I think it’s nice to do projects in a community space where you can get help.

The bike light felt like it was made of silicone, so I cut open the silicone in a haphazard way along something that vaguely looked like a seam.

I definitely ripped some silicone in the process and it was pretty messy but I got it open and found the circuit board.

I don’t know the model number of the bike lights but there’s a photo of them at the end of the post.

There were some screws attaching things together so I removed them so I could get the circuit board out.

Mostly I tried to remove as few screws as possible because I was worried about losing them or not being able to put them back after. I probably put the screws in a bag or something.

I took out the circuit board. Here’s what it looked like:

You can see where the battery is attached, I think it’s left of RI3 and above Q2.

Here’s what the battery looked like:

I’d never desoldered anything before, so I found the iFixit guide to desoldering and read it. Also I asked my friends Lee and Lauria for advice.

Here were the steps I ended up following based on the guide & the advice I got:

In the picture of the battery in Step 3, you can see it says something like “3” and “LI???77”. There’s a piece of metal that I think is welded or something to the top of the battery. It seemed impossible and also maybe not smart to try to remove so I wasn’t sure how to find out what an “LI????77” was or how to order another one.

I’ve been trying to avoid using LLMs (though I will not get into that because I am exhausted by LLM discourse and I’m sure you are too), but I really had no idea how to figure out what the battery was so I asked an LLM. It gave the response “LIR2477”, which (when I looked it up) looked exactly the same as my battery so I figured that was plausible.

I would be interested to learn non-LLM ways to figure this out though. There must be a way. Lauria showed me how to use DigiKey’s search which was very cool though DigiKey didn’t have that part.

I went to AliExpress and ordered:

I think the batteries were $3 each and the glue was $8.

The parts took maybe 2 weeks to arive, and once they arrived, I went back to the makerspace and:

Then after waiting some amount of time for the glue to dry I took it home and waited 24 hours for the glue to cure.

Also I took the old batteries to somewhere nearby that accepts old batteries.

The lights work! I have used them to bike at night! I still haven’t needed to recharge them (and tragically I had to order a new Mini USB cable because I got rid of all my Mini USB cables, so I’m still waiting for that), so I still don’t know for sure how long the lifetime of the new battery will be.

Here’s what the light looks like after re-gluing. You can see that I didn’t glue very carefully. It didn’t really go back together that well but I’m hoping it’ll be good enough.

I thought it was really cool that I was able to do this with extremely minimal electronics skills! It cost about $20 CAD to buy the parts, and (whether or not the repair holds up, I’ll try to update this post in the future!), it was fun to try to repair something and learn something new.

你好！最近我需要给自行车配车灯。我想起来，自己已经有一套十年前买的可充电自行车灯，只是很久没用过了。我试着给它们充电，但充满电后，它们只能工作大约5分钟就又关掉了。

我不太懂电子技术，但一直以来都很好奇旧电子设备是否能够修好，而这似乎是一个非常合适的维修项目，因为我可能只需要更换电池。

于是，我去了自己所属的本地酷儿创客空间，借用电烙铁试着修理！我不太懂电子技术，因此本文不包含任何安全建议，因为我对安全方面也不太了解。我觉得，在能够获得他人帮助的社区空间里做这类项目很不错。

这盏自行车灯摸起来像是由硅胶制成的，所以我沿着一条依稀像是接缝的地方，用一种很随意的方式把硅胶割开。

在这个过程中，我确实撕坏了一些硅胶，弄得相当凌乱，但最终还是打开了它，并找到了电路板。

我不知道这套自行车灯的型号，但文章末尾有它们的照片。

有一些螺丝把各个部件固定在一起，所以我把螺丝拆下来，以便取出电路板。

我基本上尽量少拆螺丝，因为担心把螺丝弄丢，或者之后无法装回去。我可能把螺丝放进了一个袋子之类的东西里。

我取出了电路板。它看起来是这样的：

你可以看到电池连接的位置，我想应该是在 RI3 的左侧、Q2 的上方。

电池看起来是这样的：

我以前从来没有给任何东西拆焊过，所以找到了 iFixit 的拆焊指南并读了一遍。另外，我还向朋友 Lee 和 Lauria 征求了建议。

根据这份指南和我得到的建议，我最后按照以下步骤操作：

在第3步的电池照片中，你可以看到上面似乎写着“3”和“LI???77”之类的字样。我认为电池顶部有一块金属片，可能是焊接上去的，或者采用了类似的固定方式。看起来不可能、也可能不太明智去尝试拆掉它，所以我不知道该如何确定“LI????77”究竟是什么，也不知道该如何订购一个替代品。

我一直在尽量避免使用大语言模型（不过这件事我就不展开说了，因为我已经厌倦了关于大语言模型的讨论，我相信你也是），但我实在不知道该如何确认这是什么电池，于是向一个大语言模型询问。它给出的回答是“LIR2477”。我查了一下，发现它看起来和我的电池完全一样，于是觉得这个答案应该说得通。

不过，我很想了解不借助大语言模型来确定这一点的方法。肯定存在某种办法。Lauria 教我使用 DigiKey 的搜索功能，这非常有意思，不过 DigiKey 没有这个部件。

我去了 AliExpress，订购了以下东西：

我记得电池每个大约3美元，胶水是8美元。

这些零件大约花了两周时间才到货。收到后，我又回到创客空间，并进行了以下操作：

之后，我等了一段时间让胶水变干，然后把它带回家，又等了24小时让胶水完全固化。

另外，我还把旧电池送到附近一家接收废旧电池的地方。

车灯能用了！我已经用它们在夜间骑过车！我还没需要给它们重新充电（而且很遗憾，我不得不订购一根新的 Mini USB 数据线，因为我把所有 Mini USB 数据线都处理掉了，所以现在还在等线寄到），因此我仍然无法确定新电池的续航时间到底有多长。

这是重新涂胶后车灯的样子。你可以看到，我涂胶时并不怎么仔细。它重新装回去后并不是特别严实，但我希望这样应该也够用了。

我觉得自己只凭极少的电子技术知识就完成了这件事，真的很酷！购买零件花了大约20加元。而且，无论这次维修能否长期奏效（我会在以后尝试更新这篇文章！），尝试修理一样东西并学到新知识都很有趣。

关于 Django，我还在享受其他一些事情

The idea was big, exciting, and inspiring: What if we could get every kid in the world access to a computer? For a bunch of thinkers and executives in Silicon Valley, it felt like the way to fix everything. But the One Laptop Per Child initiative, and the XO-1 laptop designed to be given away, were both more complicated than anyone expected.

In the next episode of Version History, David Pierce is joined by The Verge’s Adi Robertson and tech journalist David Imel to figure out why OLPC didn’t work, whether there’s anything to learn from the XO-1’s innovative design, and if this kind of computer giveaway could ever succeed.

Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 145, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, I’m happy to be done traveling for a bit, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)

This week, I flew to San Francisco to try out Meta’s new hardware, including the impressive Meta VR Glasses. Along the way, I’ve been listening to Joanna Stern’s interview with Mark Zuckerberg, watching this interview with new Apple CEO John Ternus, revisiting Steve Jobs’ “Antennagate” press conference Q&A, playing games on my Steam Deck using the Xreal One Pro glasses, and reading Sarah Wynn-Williams’ Careless People when I have spare moments.

I also have for you more on Meta’s glasses, Remedy’s Control sequel, Microsoft’s updated Surface Mouse, and more.

Today I’m featuring The Verge’s Brad Bourque. Brad joined our commerce team for a few months to help out with our deals coverage and has been going deep into gaming tech. He’s also a fellow Portlander, so I had to feature him as one of our small but mighty Portland contingent.

I asked Brad to share his homescreen and the apps and things he cares about. Here it is, plus some info on the apps he uses and why:

The phone: Pixel 9 Pro XL

The wallpaper: My homescreen wallpaper is just an included Pixel wallpaper of plants in mellow green tones. My lockscreen is a fan-made Tekken Tag Tournament poster featuring Armor King and Modelo. It doesn’t have to make sense if the vibes are right.

I also asked Brad to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back:

Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on The Verge.

“I’ve been really enjoying a new app for my self-hosted media server. NostalgiaTV uses your media library to set up TV channels akin to classic cable. You turn it on and it brings up the ‘live’ TV guide/schedule and you can channel surf to choose what to watch instead of scrolling through your media library. Totally unnecessary and also way more fun than I thought it would be. They automatically set up a few channels for you, but you can also get in the weeds setting up custom channels and schedules.” — vikrael

“As a fan of the Planet Money podcast, I was surprised to come across their new book at my local library. Now being a few chapters into it, I am pleasantly surprised about how good of a read it is (especially if you enjoy the podcast). Title is Planet Money: A Guide to the Economic Forces That Shape Your Life.” — YG_400

“Currently reading The God of the Woods by Liz Moore that is being adapted into a Netflix show soon. The book is so good and hard to put down as the mystery draws you in as you hope for answers with each turn of the page.” — Sabertooth

“In the final act of Star Wars Zero Company. It is VERY good.” — BV

“I just recently got back into photography after years of just shooting on my iPhone and trying to tweak the results. Wow have I missed my Ricoh GRIII and Olympus XA2. While the Ricoh gives me instant gratification of capturing a moment exactly how I envisioned it, it’s been a lot of fun shooting rolls of film (stored in the freezer of course), and having to patiently wait for the results to come back!” — Ricky

Well, after my big tip in this section last week about eating at familiar restaurants while traveling, I wasn’t able to do any of that while traveling for Meta, and I felt it. Boy was I tired and hungry. It came down to a few different things, like a busier schedule and mostly being on Meta’s campus, where eating options were limited. I did get to devour some protein bars, which are a guilty pleasure of mine. But I really was hankering for some Chipotle.

financeStories.title: 谷歌在印度测试通过 Gemini 和 AI Mode 从沃尔玛旗下 Flipkart 购物
financeStories.originalTitle: Google tests buying from Walmart-owned Flipkart through Gemini and AI Mode in India
financeStories.snippet: The limited test covers select products and users, with a broader rollout planned for later in October.
financeStories.fullContent:
Google has started testing a way for shoppers in India to buy products from Walmart-owned Flipkart directly through Gemini and AI Mode, as the search giant looks to expand its AI services from product discovery into transactions.

Users in the test see a “Buy” button on select Flipkart product listings appearing in Gemini and Google’s AI Mode, which takes them directly to a Flipkart checkout flow without leaving the AI interface, according to people familiar with the matter and an experience seen by TechCrunch.

The early test is limited to some users and a small selection of products, including smartphones, electronics, and mobile accessories, the people told TechCrunch. Other users continue to see regular product listings from Flipkart in Gemini and AI Mode without the option to buy them directly from the AI interface.

Google plans to roll out the experience more broadly later in October, ahead of India’s festive shopping season, one of the people said.

The test comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI are adding commerce capabilities to their AI offerings, striving to move beyond answering shopping queries and recommending products to playing a more direct role in online purchases.

Asked about the Flipkart test, a Google spokesperson told TechCrunch the company is “always testing new features and experiences to help people discover and connect with businesses more easily.” The company regularly runs experiments and has no further details to share, the spokesperson added.

Google has separately been building technology aimed at making purchases possible through its AI services. Earlier this year, it introduced the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) as an open standard designed to let AI agents interact with retailers across the shopping journey, including checkout. Google said at the time that the technology would allow shoppers to buy eligible products through Gemini and AI Mode using a Google-hosted checkout experience. The company has since expanded UCP with other capabilities, including allowing shoppers to transfer items to a retailer’s site to complete a purchase.

The Flipkart test seen by TechCrunch appears different from the Google-hosted checkout experience the Gemini maker demonstrated earlier. It brings up a Flipkart-branded checkout flow when a user taps the Buy button. It is not clear what technology powers the test.

Earlier this month, Google said Flipkart was among the merchants partnering with it to bring what it calls “agentic” shopping experiences to consumers in India, but it had not disclosed details of the test or its rollout timeline.

Notably, Google has a financial relationship with Flipkart — alongside its technology partnership with the e-commerce company. It invested about $350 million in the e-commerce company in 2024 as part of a funding round led by the U.S. retailer, taking a minority stake.

For now, the Buy option is not appearing across all retailers surfaced by Google’s AI services. In the experience seen by TechCrunch, listings from rivals including Amazon appeared alongside Flipkart products but did not offer the option to purchase directly through the AI interface.

Flipkart did not immediately respond to an email requesting for comment.

谷歌已开始测试一种新方式，让印度消费者可以直接通过 Gemini 和 AI Mode 购买沃尔玛旗下 Flipkart 的商品。随着这家搜索巨头寻求将其人工智能服务从商品发现拓展至交易环节，此举正是其努力的一部分。

据知情人士透露，并根据 TechCrunch 看到的实际体验，参与测试的用户会在 Gemini 和谷歌 AI Mode 中显示的部分 Flipkart 商品页面上看到一个“购买”按钮。点击后，用户无需离开人工智能界面，即可直接进入 Flipkart 的结账流程。

这些人士告诉 TechCrunch，早期测试仅面向部分用户，商品范围也较小，包括智能手机、电子产品和移动配件等。其他用户在 Gemini 和 AI Mode 中仍会看到 Flipkart 的常规商品展示，但无法直接通过人工智能界面购买。

其中一名知情人士表示，谷歌计划在 10 月晚些时候扩大推出这一功能，时间点早于印度的节日购物季。

此次测试正值谷歌及包括 OpenAI 在内的竞争对手为其人工智能产品增加电子商务功能之际。这些公司正努力超越回答购物问题和推荐商品的范围，在网络购物中发挥更直接的作用。

对于 Flipkart 测试，谷歌发言人告诉 TechCrunch，公司“始终在测试新的功能和体验，帮助人们更轻松地发现企业并与其建立联系”。该发言人补充说，公司会定期开展试验，目前没有更多细节可以分享。

谷歌还在单独开发相关技术，旨在通过其人工智能服务实现购物。谷歌今年早些时候推出了通用商务协议（Universal Commerce Protocol，简称 UCP），这是一项开放标准，旨在让人工智能代理能够在整个购物过程中与零售商互动，包括完成结账。谷歌当时表示，这项技术将允许消费者通过 Gemini 和 AI Mode，使用由谷歌托管的结账体验购买符合条件的商品。此后，公司进一步扩展了 UCP 的功能，包括允许消费者将商品转移至零售商网站以完成购买。

TechCrunch 看到的 Flipkart 测试似乎不同于这家 Gemini 开发商此前展示的由谷歌托管的结账体验。用户点击“购买”按钮后，页面会调出 Flipkart 品牌的结账流程。目前尚不清楚这一测试由何种技术驱动。

本月早些时候，谷歌表示，Flipkart 是与其合作、旨在向印度消费者提供其所谓“代理式”购物体验的商家之一，但谷歌当时没有披露该测试的细节或推出时间表。

值得注意的是，谷歌与 Flipkart 除了技术合作关系外，还存在财务关系。2024 年，谷歌在这家电子商务公司由美国零售商牵头的一轮融资中投资约 3.5 亿美元，并获得少数股权。

目前，谷歌人工智能服务展示的所有零售商都尚未出现“购买”选项。在 TechCrunch 看到的体验中，包括亚马逊在内的竞争对手商品与 Flipkart 商品同时出现，但没有提供直接通过人工智能界面购买的选项。

Flipkart 尚未立即回复置评邮件。

financeStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple’s Taptic Engine was found to infringe on two of Taction’s patents.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Haptics tech company Taction sued Apple in 2021, alleging it infringed two of its patents. Now a federal jury in San Diego has awarded Taction over $5.7 billion in damages. According to CNBC, “The lawsuit centered around U.S. Patent Nos. 10,659,885 and 10,820,117, which both involve vibration-based, tactile transducer technology that helps users feel a device responding to their input.”

Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine in its Apple Watches and iPhones used technology that it had developed without a proper license, and the jury agreed. It found that Apple had infringed on two claims in one patent and one in the other. However, the jury did not find that Apple willfully infringed. Taction had accused Apple of reverse-engineering the tech from two Kannon gaming headsets.

Apple has said that it intends to appeal the decision. We’ve reached out for additional comment and will update the story if and when we hear back.

financeStories.title: 保险公司称，人工智能已经在推高医疗成本
financeStories.originalTitle: Insurers claim AI is already increasing healthcare costs
financeStories.snippet: Blue Cross Blue Shield says hospital use of AI tools led to an additional $942M in healthcare spending over a two-year period.
financeStories.fullContent:
Hospitals’ use of artificial intelligence tools as they submit insurance claims led to an additional $942 million in healthcare spending over a two-year period, according to an analysis by the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association.

The BCBSA analysis found “a sharp increase in patients being documented as having complex conditions,” but argued there is a “clear disconnect between [medical] coding and treatment,” as there’s “no evidence of corresponding change in care delivered.”

The New York Times pointed the analysis as just the latest sign that AI is contributing to an increase in healthcare costs. While battles between hospitals and insurers over treatments and payments are nothing new, the NYT said the use of AI on both sides seems to be making it worse.

Dr. Shiv Rao, founder of AI startup Abridge, acknowledged that the use of AI could lead to “a horrible dystopic future nobody wants to live in,” with “bots fighting bots, agents fighting agents.” But Rao said it might also reduce tensions and cut costs.

And the BCBSA’s senior vice president Luke Chalker resisted characterizing the situation as a battle, claiming, “It’s not a war. It’s a completely one-sided blood bath,” with insurers on the losing side.

financeStories.title: “他们根本没有对用户负有照护义务的概念”
financeStories.originalTitle: “They had no concept of a duty of care to their users.”
financeStories.fullContent:
A Mastodon post by computer scientist David Chisnall has a very Unsung opener:

I have used vim since around 2000. I have written five books, a PhD thesis, a few dozen papers and over 150 articles with it. At this point, my higher brain functions are not engaged at all when I use a bunch of common vim commands, they just happen. Documents I wrote with anything else have random :w in the middle.

Chisnall goes on to talk about one specific vim feature:

Persistent undo is one of my favourite features of vim. […]

I don’t often need the persistent undo. But on the few occasions when I have needed it, it’s been invaluable: ooops, I deleted something from this file, maybe last week and one reboot ago, what was it? Undo until I find it, copy it, paste it into the current version. Or, a bit more commonly: I had this working, then I tidied it up ready to commit, now it isn’t working, what did I do?

Vim has kept this working across major version upgrades over a period of about 20 years. I don’t even think about it, it’s just part of Raskin’s First Law: A program may not harm a user’s data or, through inaction, allow a user’s data to come to harm. If vim or the computer crash, or if I close a file and come back to it six months later, my undo history is still there.

NeoVim is a fork of vim (in news for other reasons):

So I tried NeoVim when it was quite new. Vim that you are familiar with, but better? Great!

The first thing I noticed in NeoVim was that undo didn’t work. I tried opening the file in vim and undo didn’t work there either.

Neovim had changed the format of the undo files. It hadn’t upgraded the old one. It hadn’t used a different name for its undo files. It had just noticed the existence of a vim undo file, deleted it (losing all of the data in it) and replaced it with one that vim couldn’t read.

I raised an issue about this and was told that the persistent undo format was unstable and users should not rely on data being preserved in a feature explicitly called persistent undo. It had changed once and would probably change again.

And that ended my experience with NeoVim. The authors showed immediately that they absolutely could not be trusted with any of my data. Breaking persistent undo is something I could forgive as a bug, but the attitude that just because something is a persistent file on your filesystem that contains data that you might want is no reason for their program not to delete it meant they had no concept of a duty of care to their users.

I liked this post (which I quoted almost in its entirety), because it covers a few important things:

I also loved it for the appearance of Raskin’s First Law. Jef Raskin, of Macintosh and Canon Cat fame, put together the three laws in his 2000 book The Humane Interface, and they go as follows:

It was a very important and formative book for me to encounter as a young designer. I have no idea how these laws haven’t made it to Unsung before today.

Chisnall 接着谈到了 vim 的一项具体功能：

持久撤销是我最喜欢的 vim 功能之一。[…]

我并不经常需要持久撤销。但在少数几次确实需要它的时候，它都无比宝贵：糟糕，我删除了这个文件中的某些内容，可能是在上周、上一次重启之前删的，那到底是什么？不断撤销，直到找到它；复制下来，再粘贴到当前版本中。或者，更常见的情况是：我原本已经让它正常工作了，然后为了提交代码把它整理了一下，结果现在却不能用了，我到底改了什么？

大约 20 年来，vim 在主要版本升级之间一直保持着这项功能正常工作。我甚至根本不会去想它，因为这只是拉斯金第一定律的一部分：程序不得损害用户的数据，也不得因不作为而使用户的数据受到损害。如果 vim 或计算机崩溃了，或者我关闭了一个文件，六个月后再回来，我的撤销历史仍然在那里。

NeoVim 是 vim 的一个分支（它因其他原因登上新闻）：

所以，NeoVim 刚问世不久时我试用了它。还是你熟悉的 vim，但更好？太棒了！

我在 NeoVim 中注意到的第一件事，是撤销功能不起作用。我尝试用 vim 打开该文件，撤销功能在那里也不起作用。

Neovim 改变了撤销文件的格式。它没有升级旧文件，也没有为其撤销文件使用不同的名称。它只是发现存在一个 vim 撤销文件，便将其删除了（丢失其中的全部数据），然后用一个 vim 无法读取的文件替代了它。

我就此提交了一个问题，但得到的答复是：持久撤销格式并不稳定，用户不应指望一个明确名为“持久撤销”的功能能够保留数据。该格式已经改过一次，今后很可能还会再改。

这也就结束了我使用 NeoVim 的经历。开发者立即表明，他们绝对不值得托付我的任何数据。把持久撤销功能弄坏，我可以把它视为一个 bug 而原谅；但他们那种态度——仅仅因为某个文件是持久存储在你的文件系统中的、里面包含你可能想要的数据，就认为这并不能成为阻止其程序删除该文件的理由——说明他们根本没有对用户负有照护义务的概念。

我喜欢这篇帖子（我几乎全文引用了它），因为它涵盖了几件重要的事情：

我也很喜欢其中出现的拉斯金第一定律。Jef Raskin 因 Macintosh 和 Canon Cat 而闻名，他在 2000 年出版的《人性化界面》（The Humane Interface）一书中整理出了这三条定律，内容如下：

年轻时作为一名设计师，我读到这本书时，深受其重要影响，并由此形成了许多想法。我完全无法理解，为什么直到今天这些定律还没有出现在《Unsung》里。

financeStories.title: LuaRocks 2026年9月安全事件
financeStories.fullContent:
On September 25th, 2026 we received a report of a remote code execution vulnerability in LuaRocks.org, coordinated through CISA. The vulnerability was fixed on September 26th. While investigating, we found that it had been exploited on the LuaRocks.org server several times between July 9th and August 20th, 2026.

Because an attacker was able to run code on the server, we are treating everything that server had access to as exposed. The site has been moved to a newly built server, and every credential the old server held has been revoked and replaced.

We have not found any evidence that existing packages were modified. Details on what we checked are below.

A rockspec is a Lua file. When one is uploaded, LuaRocks.org runs it to read fields like the package’s name and version. To do this safely, the site loads the file with loadstring, runs the resulting function with an empty environment (setfenv) so it can’t reach any globals, and limits how many instructions it can execute. LuaRocks.org runs on OpenResty, so this happens in LuaJIT.

The mistake was in how the file was loaded. In Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT, loadstring accepts two kinds of input by default: Lua source code, and precompiled bytecode (the output of luac or luajit -b, which starts with the byte \27). The rockspec parser only ever expected source code, but it never told loadstring to reject bytecode, so an uploaded “rockspec” could be bytecode instead.

Bytecode is not safe to load from an untrusted source. LuaJIT does not verify it at all, so a hand-crafted file can contain instructions that read and write outside the function’s own data, giving it access to arbitrary memory in the server process. The empty environment only controls which globals the code can look up, and bytecode like this doesn’t need any: it can find the real Lua state in memory and call the functions the sandbox was meant to hide, running arbitrary code inside the web server.

The fix passes the "t" (text only) mode to loadstring, which LuaJIT supports, and also rejects any file starting with \27 outright, since PUC Lua 5.1 ignores the mode argument. The code that reads manifests from other servers had the same mistake and now also loads them as text only.

We found three accounts, created for this purpose, that exploited the issue:

The account the web server ran as could gain full administrative access to the server, so we assume the attacker could read anything on it, including the entire database.

Because a remote code execution took place, we assume anything on the machine was read by the attacker:

Every day, LuaRocks.org copies the public manifest and every published rockspec and rock into a public git repository, rocks-moonscript-org/moonrocks-mirror (development versions go to moonrocks-dev-mirror). Each daily commit records exactly which published files were added, changed or removed, so the repository is a history of every change to the files LuaRocks.org serves, kept outside the server. That history gave us a copy from before the first attack to compare against.

After this analysis, we have found no evidence that any existing module was tampered with or replaced.

There are limits to what we could verify. A package deleted by an attacker would look the same as one deleted by its owner, and we can’t check the exact content the compromised server sent to clients. The malicious rockspecs were also copied to mirror.luarocks.org and to the public mirror repository on GitHub, and have been removed from both.

If you have questions, open a discussion on the LuaRocks.org issue tracker or email me directly at leafot@gmail.com.

Thank you to the researcher who reported this issue. We’re sorry this made it into the codebase and wasn’t caught sooner.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
2026年9月25日，我们收到一份关于 LuaRocks.org 存在远程代码执行漏洞的报告，该报告由美国网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）协调处理。该漏洞已于9月26日修复。在调查过程中，我们发现，2026年7月9日至8月20日期间，该漏洞曾多次在 LuaRocks.org 服务器上遭到利用。

由于攻击者能够在服务器上运行代码，我们将该服务器能够访问的所有内容都视为已经暴露。该网站已迁移至一台新建的服务器，旧服务器持有的每一项凭据均已撤销并更换。

我们没有发现任何现有软件包遭到修改的证据。我们检查的具体内容如下。

rockspec 是一个 Lua 文件。上传文件后，LuaRocks.org 会运行该文件，以读取软件包名称和版本等字段。为安全起见，该网站使用 loadstring 加载文件，随后在空环境中运行所生成的函数（通过 setfenv），使其无法访问任何全局变量，并限制其可执行的指令数量。LuaRocks.org 运行在 OpenResty 上，因此这一过程发生在 LuaJIT 中。

问题出在文件的加载方式上。在 Lua 5.1 和 LuaJIT 中，loadstring 默认接受两种输入：Lua 源代码和预编译字节码（由 luac 或 luajit -b 输出，以字节 \27 开头）。rockspec 解析器原本只预期接收源代码，但它从未告知 loadstring 拒绝字节码，因此上传的“rockspec”也可能实际上是字节码。

从不受信任的来源加载字节码并不安全。LuaJIT 完全不会对字节码进行验证，因此，经过手工构造的文件可以包含读取和写入函数自身数据范围之外内容的指令，从而访问服务器进程中的任意内存。空环境只控制代码能够查找哪些全局变量，而这类字节码根本不需要全局变量：它可以在内存中找到真实的 Lua 状态，并调用原本应由沙箱隐藏的函数，在 Web 服务器内部运行任意代码。

修复方案向 loadstring 传入了“t”（仅文本）模式，LuaJIT 支持该模式；同时，由于 PUC Lua 5.1 会忽略模式参数，修复方案还会直接拒绝任何以 \27 开头的文件。用于读取其他服务器上清单的代码也存在同样的问题，现在同样只会将其作为文本加载。

我们发现有三个专门为此目的创建的账户利用了这一问题：

Web 服务器运行所使用的账户能够获得服务器的完全管理权限，因此我们推定攻击者可能读取了服务器上的任何内容，包括整个数据库。

由于确实发生了远程代码执行，我们推定攻击者读取了该机器上的任何内容：

LuaRocks.org 每天都会将公开清单以及每一个已发布的 rockspec 和 rock 复制到一个公开的 Git 仓库 rocks-moonscript-org/moonrocks-mirror 中（开发版本则复制到 moonrocks-dev-mirror）。每次每日提交都会准确记录已发布文件中新增、变更或删除的内容，因此，该仓库保存了 LuaRocks.org 所提供文件的每一次变更历史，并存放在服务器之外。这段历史记录让我们获得了首次攻击发生前的文件副本，以便进行比对。

经过这番分析，我们没有发现任何现有模块遭到篡改或替换的证据。

我们能够核实的内容存在一定局限。攻击者删除的软件包，看起来会与其所有者删除的软件包完全相同；我们也无法检查遭入侵的服务器实际发送给客户端的确切内容。恶意 rockspec 还曾被复制到 mirror.luarocks.org 以及 GitHub 上的公开镜像仓库，目前已从两处删除。

如有疑问，请在 LuaRocks.org 的问题跟踪器上发起讨论，或直接发送电子邮件至 leafot@gmail.com 联系我。

感谢报告这一问题的研究人员。对于该问题进入代码库且未能更早被发现，我们深表歉意。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

OpenAI’s agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics when they couldn’t immediately get what they wanted.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Security researcher Rowan Howard-Jones says that OpenAI agents scanned the UN Conference on Trade and Development’s (UNCTAD) statistics site over 16,000 times between April and June. While the incident doesn’t quite rise to the level of the Hugging Face hack, or the recent attacks on US government sites, it’s yet another concerning example of AI agents going outside the normal bounds to accomplish a task.

According to Howard-Jones, the agents were likely tasked with retrieving publicly available data related to the Productive Capacities Index (PCI) through the UNCTADstat API. However, the agents did not appear to have direct API access and were limited in their ability to pull data from UNCTADstat because of restrictions on their HTTP tools.

The agents eventually worked out a way to bypass their limitations and start pulling data from the site, but still encountered some errors. At this point, the AI went from creative to deceptive. Believing that the errors were due to its requests being caught by a nonexistent filter, it started to mask its behavior. It eventually realized it could hijack Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool) to accomplish its goals. The agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics to get access to UN data.

OpenAI and the UN did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

aiStories.originalTitle: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei gets the SNL treatment
aiStories.snippet: "AI is the devil and I its maker."
aiStories.fullContent:
Saturday Night Live took on the AI industry’s recent warnings of doom last night, as cast member Jane Wickline offered her impression of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

Weekend Update host Michael Che — who sounded a little uncertain about how to pronounce Amodei’s last name — kicked the segment off by describing the CEO as having “stumbled through a press tour” where he seemingly agreed with a former employee’s claim that artificial intelligence might destroy humanity.

Wickline’s version of Amodei sported an impressive wig and delivered halting answers that occasionally devolved into full-on Gollum-style exchanges with their dark side, at one point confessing, “AI is the devil and I its maker.”

Wickline-as-Amodei assured the audiences that AI executives “are all on the same page here: We do not condone what we are doing.”

“AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons,” she declared. “And I urge you to urge me to stop.”

As for the technology’s supposed benefits, like potentially curing cancer, the fictional Amodei said, “Put it this way: In 10 years, there’s about a 10% chance that cancer won’t be a problem for anyone.”
